properties.areaDesc: Cameron, TX
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 7 at 6:50PM CDT until October 7 at 8:45PM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...East Central Cameron County in deep south Texas...

* WHEN...Until 845 PM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Overflowing poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 649 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
South Padre Island, Holly Beach, Laguna Vista Police Department,
Laguna Heights, Port Isabel High School, Port Isabel City Hall,
Port Isabel Lighthouse, Port Isabel Fire And Police Department,
South Padre Island Convention Center, Beach Access Five, Beach
Access Four, South Padre Island Birding Center, Garria Elementary
School, Beach Access Six, Washington Park, South Padre Island
Police Department, U.s. Coast Guard Station, Bayview and Port
Isabel--Laguna Heights.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 845 PM CDT THIS EVENING

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 7 at 12:45PM SST by NWS Pago Pago  AS
properties.description:
ESFPPG

An active trough to the north is projected to drift southward and
move over the territory by around Tuesday of next week. This
trough is likely to remain strong and active through the duration
of next week, and may even intensify with embedded low pressure
centers. Widespread showers may be heavy and persistent at times
with the possibility of thunderstorms Tuesday through the weekend.
Widespread flash flooding may occur from this rainfall.
Landslides will be possible along steep mountainous terrain.
While there is still uncertainty in the exact magnitude and
duration of rainfall, plan now for wet conditions next Tuesday
through Sunday.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through our
internet page (www.weather.gov/ppg), local media, social media,
and our NOAA Radio broadcasts.

NWSheadline: Flash Flooding and landslide potential for Tuesday through next Sunday

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 7 at 7:36PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed to Moderate severity for the following
rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to continue a steady rise
through this week due to northerly winds and repeated rounds of heavy
rainfall across the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w, Above Lake Harney,
Sanford, Deland, Astor...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.0 feet, Water approaches or may enter lowest homes
on or near Wildhog Road and nearby canals. Flooding reaches the
parking lot of the Juno Trail Apartments. Flooding on portions of
Alligator Road and Holiday Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue
Creek are flooded. Roads at Astor Landing Campground and Lake
Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood. Water enters lower homes closest
to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:30 PM EDT Wednesday the stage was 2.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 6:30 PM EDT Wednesday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 2.8 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 3.1
feet on 09/10/2005.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 1100 AM EDT.
